name: South China Sea
genZNote: The South China Sea carries a wildly disproportionate share of the world's shipping for how often you actually hear it mentioned outside the news about territorial disputes.

sections.heading: 🌊 Location & Ocean Connection
bullets: A marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean, bounded by mainland Southeast Asia to the west, the Philippines to the east, and southern China/Taiwan to the north.
Connects to the Strait of Malacca (and onward to the Indian Ocean) in the southwest, making it the middle link in the main Europe/Middle East–East Asia sea route.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Countries Bordering It
bullets: China, Taiwan, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei, Indonesia (its northern waters) and Singapore (at its south-western edge near the Strait of Malacca).

sections.heading: 🚢 Ports & Trade Routes
bullets: One of the world's busiest sea lanes by shipping volume, carrying a very large share of global trade between East Asia and the rest of the world.
Major ports on or near it: Singapore, Ho Chi Minh City, Manila, Hong Kong, Guangzhou/Shenzhen.
It is the essential middle segment connecting the Strait of Malacca to the wider Pacific shipping network used by China, Japan and South Korea.

sections.heading: 🐠 Ecology & Notable Geopolitical Facts
bullets: Contains rich fishing grounds and significant offshore oil and gas reserves, along with extensive coral reef systems around the Spratly and Paracel Islands.
Subject to overlapping territorial claims among several bordering countries — an important, sensitive geopolitical topic that is presented here only as a geographic fact, not a political judgement.
Its coral reefs face pressure from land reclamation, warming waters and overfishing.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The South China Sea is a marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean between mainland Southeast Asia, the Philippines and China, and one of the world's busiest shipping lanes.
keyFacts: Marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean.
Borders China, Taiwan, Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei, Indonesia, Singapore.
Connects the Strait of Malacca to the wider Pacific shipping network.
Contains the Spratly and Paracel Island groups.
commonConfusion: The South China Sea and the East China Sea are two different seas — the South China Sea is further south, near Southeast Asia, not near Japan/Korea.

highYieldFacts: South China Sea = marginal sea of the Pacific, borders Southeast Asia + China + Philippines.
Links the Strait of Malacca to East Asia's Pacific shipping routes.
Spratly and Paracel Islands are within it.
commonTraps: Don't confuse it with the East China Sea, which sits between China, Japan and South Korea.
mustRemember: South China Sea = key middle link between the Strait of Malacca and East Asia's ports.
